articles.title: Gérard Depardieu and Michel Houellebecq investigated over on-set rape and assault allegations
articles.summary: Actor and author are alleged to have attacked and gang-raped a woman while filming together in 2018. French police are investigating allegations that the actor Gérard Depardieu and the author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman during a 2018 film shoot.
body: The alleged attack took place in December 2018 during the shooting of Thalasso, a film starring the two men as versions of themselves who meet at a health spa and have long philosophical conversations while in white bath-robes.
Two sources following the case confirmed to Agence France-Presse on Friday that a police investigation was under way.
The investigative website Mediapart reported this week that an actor, given the pseudonym Alexandra, had made a complaint to police in 2025.

Alexandra, an eastern European actor and dancer who was 32 at the time and working in France, told Mediapart that she was attacked by Depardieu and Houellebecq as they pinned her down during one scene and while cameras filmed.

articles.title: Marvel’s ‘Blade’ Director Exited Failed Movie Because ‘Life’s Too Short to Make S— Films’ and It Was ‘Dangerous’ Working ‘Without a Proper Script’
articles.summary: Bassam Tariq revealed in a new interview with The New Arab that the biggest lesson he learned as the original director of Marvel’s failed “Blade” movie is “life’s too short to make shit films.” “It was funny and strange to start casting and building without a proper script,” Tariq said abot his…
body: “If you’re the bearer of bad news to your actors, but you’re not the one making any of these decisions — and it’s actually coming from a corporate entity — that’s not a great way to be a director,” the director continued. “I know some people can take that and run with it, but I learned I was losing credibility with my actors, and it wasn’t a healthy way to operate as a filmmaker. Life’s too short to make shit films, so that was my big lesson: I have to have full control over my script. If we disagree, it’s between them and me. It’s quite sad because we had such high hopes for what we wanted to build.”

Marvel originally announced “Blade” at Comic-Con in July 2019 with Oscar winner Mahershala Ali set to star in the title role. Tariq (who went on to direct Ali in “Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother”) was the first director to join the movie, but he exited in September 2022 roughly two months before it was set to begin shooting. Yann Demange stepped in as the movie’s director after Tariq’s exit, but Demange ended up dropping out in June 2024.

articles.title: Egyptian Actor Asser Yassin on His Dark Role in Psychological Thriller ‘Asal Ahmar,’ Alongside Hend Sabry: ‘I Like to Indulge in Intense Characters’
articles.summary: Fresh off receiving the Faten Hamama Excellence Award at the 47th Cairo Intl. Film Festival, Egyptian actor Asser Yassin is looking ahead. For the star, whose career spans two decades across independent cinema, commercial films and television, the recognition comes at a moment of renewed ambition…
body: Rather than viewing the honor as a culmination of his career, Yassin sees it as inspiration to continue evolving. “Doubt is always there. Hesitation is always there,” he says. “Faith is the light. And this is a proof of that light.”

That ambition is already taking shape in his latest project, “Asal Ahmar” (“Red Honey”), a psychological thriller adapted from a novel by Egyptian writer Ibrahim Eissa. The series reunites Yassin with Egyptian-Tunisian actress Hend Sabry and marks his first collaboration with director Mariam Ahmadi, with whom he says he has long wanted to work.

Drawn to the intensity of the source material, Yassin describes a role with “a very dark side” that explores themes of motherhood, delving into his character’s relationship with his mother. “I always like, every now and then, to indulge in an intense character,” he explains.

For the actor, the role also represents an opportunity to apply lessons learned over the course of his career, particularly when it comes to separating himself from emotionally demanding performances.

articles.title: Delays mean Robert Pattinson doesn’t have to do a third Batman movie. DC Studios had better persuade him – and fast
articles.summary: The actor’s new role as James Bond could be bad news for DC, as a new owner, new chief and new director already threaten to shake and stir Gotham’s distinctive hero. Can one actor play both Batman and James Bond?
body: Among all the furore over Pattinson’s appointment, it would have been easy to miss some rather less cheering news for the citizens of Gotham. According to the Wrap, delays to The Batman: Part II have freed the actor from his contractual obligation to make a third film. The sequel is now due in February 2028, almost six years after the first instalment. He could still sign a new deal, of course, but Warner Bros will have to persuade its caped crusader to stick around.

Four years ago, when The Batman hit cinemas to a chorus of critical acclaim for its brooding blend of detective noir and superhero spectacle, there would have been little question that the studio was all in. The film took more than $770m worldwide and seemed to promise a trilogy that might one day give Christopher Nolan’s Dark Knight triptych a run for its money. But much has changed since then.

articles.title: Hello Sunshine’s Lauren Neustadter Stepping Down at Year’s End (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The longtime president of film and television is leaving after nearly a decade at Reese Witherspoon’s company and on the heels of a recent ownership change.
body: Changes continue at Reese Witherspoon ’s Hello Sunshine, where the company’s top creative executive, Lauren Neustadter, is stepping down at year’s end. The longtime collaborators announced the move on Friday afternoon.

“Building Hello Sunshine alongside Reese and our incredible team has been the privilege of a lifetime,” added Neustadter. “I’m deeply proud of all the shows and movies we’ve made, the doors we’ve opened for new voices, and the ways we have put women in the spotlight both in front of and behind the camera. I am grateful for every moment of it, and I will always be cheering for Hello Sunshine.”

Her departure comes during a period of transition for Hello Sunshine. In October, Witherspoon teamed up with Mediawan to buy the company back from Candle Media. Hello Sunshine, which Witherspoon founded with Seth Rodsky in 2016, was acquired by the Blackstone-backed company in 2021 in a deal valued at $900 million.

articles.title: ‘The hand of god’ and all that: Lineker, Shilton et al look back at 1986 England-Argentina clash – The Match review
articles.summary: Argentinian co-directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco work hard to appear impartial in account that situates the game in a long continuum of conflict. Here is a football documentary that is a cut above the drain-clogging content that loiters in streaming platforms everywhere.
body: Over and above football matters, it’s clear to see that there were bigger things at stake. Rather obviously, it happened only four years after the Falklands war, which thoroughly poisoned already tense relations between Britain and Argentina. The Match situates the 1986 clash as part of a continuum of strife, dating back at least to the arrival in 1765 of a British sea captain, John Byron, on the Falklands to claim them for Britain. Other key moments: Argentina’s Antonio Rattín getting sent off during the 1966 World Cup, and Maradona being invited on stage by Queen to sing Another One Bites the Dust during their mammoth 1981 South American tour.

body: Catherine Zeta-Jones's daughter has said her parents warned her people might have "preconceived notions" about her embarking on an acting career, as she shared her views on the "nepo baby" label.
Carys Douglas, 23, made her stage debut this year, playing the lead role of Nina in Anton Chekhov's The Seagull in Brooklyn, New York.

Zeta-Jones, who is married to Michael Douglas, son of Hollywood star Kirk, previously said the "nepo baby" term was "horrific". It refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.
But the young actor said her parents taught her to build her "own identity" and she has learned how to deal with the "pressure".

articles.title: Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Is The Darkest Movie In The Series
articles.summary: Sunrise on the Reaping is the darkest Hunger Games movie yet - and that's saying something in a franchise centered around children dying horribly.
body: The following post contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping."

It's rare for a franchise to get better after 4 or 5 movies, especially when they are prequels that explore questions no one needed answered. It didn't work for "Star Wars," it didn't work for "Harry Potter," and it shouldn't work for "Hunger Games." At best, these prequels just introduced characters that don't matter in the large scheme of things because everything they do or accomplish gets erased in the original story, at worst they try so hard to answer questions no one cares about that it ends up tarnishing the original work.

And yet, when it comes to "Hunger Games," not only has the franchise improved with time, but the two spin-off prequels are arguably better than even the original series. The latest film, "Sunrise on the Reaping" deepens what came before, while introducing new characters that are as engaging as those we know and add to the larger worldbuilding of Panem. Or, as /Film's review puts it, "Beyond the shock value, this story remains human, emotional, and gripping from beginning to end."
points: Sunrise on the Reaping is the darkest Hunger Games movie yet - and that's saying something in a franchise centered around children dying horribly.
